text:
sam: Heads-up — Deploybot just paused the rollout after the incident spike in eu-west. It flagged increased 5xx rate on canary. Need quick call: rollback, pin, or keep paused and re-run canary?

deploybot: [automated] rollout paused for release r-2026-04-13. Reason: canary error-rate > 2% over 5m. To resume: @eng-releases run `deployctl resume r-2026-04-13` after confirmation.

linda: What services are affected? user-facing inference and routing-mesh, right?

maria: Correct — routing-mesh errors seem tied to kvcache eviction patch in model-serving. Canary is v1.4.3-hotpatch. Non-canary traffic still on v1.4.2.

alex: Proposal: pin production to v1.4.2 (sticky pin) and keep canary quarantined. Prepare rollback plan for v1.4.3 if we can't reproduce quick.

sam: Agree. If we pin, we should also push brief release-note deprecation line and schedule a follow-up patch release.

ops-oncall-bot: Suggested steps:
1) `deployctl pin --release r-2026-04-13 --version v1.4.2` 
2) `deployctl quarantine --canary r-2026-04-13` 
3) Notify customers via status page if we expect >30m impact

maria: I'll run the pin now and open a rollback PR. Quick checklist I'm pushing into the thread: 
```
- Pin prod to v1.4.2 (complete)
- Quarantine canary v1.4.3 (complete)
- Re-run canary with disabled kvcache patch (experiment)
- If error persists -> rollback image tag on model-serving -> run validation load test
- Update release notes + changelog + incident reference
```

alex: For rollback commands (if needed):
`kubectl -n serving set image deploy/model-serving model-serving=redwood/model-serving:v1.4.2`
`kubectl -n serving rollout status deploy/model-serving`

sam: I'm updating the release notes now — short blurb: "Rolled back v1.4.3 canary due to elevated 5xx on routing-mesh; production pinned to v1.4.2 pending investigation." Will push to /release-notes and link here.

maria: Pushed release-note draft: https://git.internal/redwood/release-notes/r-2026-04-13.md (added incident id INC-2026-142). I'll also tag @platform-eng for kernel/kv-cache review.

linda: Any estimate on lift? If we pin and quarantine, we can probably have ops stable in ~15-30m, assuming no cascading failures.

sam: OK go ahead with pin + quarantine. If anyone sees unexplained rollforward attempts, react here immediately. I'll also notify product/CS about the short delay and the pinned version. :thumbsup:

deploybot: [automated] action taken: production pinned to v1.4.2 by maria at 1729982650. Canary quarantine set for r-2026-04-13.

maria: Done. I'll follow up with a postmortem draft once we have root cause.
